title: Off-by-1 Labs Research: AI-generated vulnerability patches require human review | 1Password
excerpt: Defenders are increasingly turning to LLMs to to generate vulnerability patches. But our research showed that LLMs only successfully generate patches (without materially changing application behavior) 26% of the time.
content_html:
We studied what happens when Large Language Models (LLMs) generate vulnerability patches for recently disclosed, complex vulnerabilities. Our data shows that LLMs produce Fix-Like Artifacts with Embedded Defects (FLAWED) 53.9% of the time when complex patches are required.

By sharing the results of our research, our goal is to provide defenders with the tooling and methodology necessary to improve vulnerability remediation outcomes at scale. Along with this blog, we are releasing our tooling, datasets, and an in-depth research paper to share what we’ve learned.

With models and agentic harnesses now performing impactful vulnerability discovery at scale, as recently witnessed with Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, defenders are naturally turning to AI agents to generate vulnerability patches. Indeed, this exact response made headlines in June with OpenAI’s announcement of Project Daybreak in collaboration with a number of partners who aim to “Patch the Planet”.

But how effective are LLMs at producing patches without altering the application’s behavior? Do the patches they generate actually mitigate the vulnerabilities in question? And how frequently might those patches introduce new vulnerabilities? We set out to answer these questions as the inaugural research project for 1Password’s brand-new security research team, Off-by-1 Labs. The paper's title is Frontier Models’ Vulnerability Patches are Often F.L.A.W.E.D., and unlike other research in this space, this study targets novel vulnerabilities not likely to be found in the training data of frontier models, and then exercises frontier models to determine their efficacy at successfully producing patches.

Across six recently-disclosed CVEs, we produced 6,080 patches using two frontier, cyber-capable reasoning models. The average success rate for generating a patch that fully resolved the vulnerability (without materially changing application behavior) was just 26.0%. Patches that successfully resolved the vulnerability, but altered the application’s behavior in the process, occurred 20.1% of the time. Examples of application behavior changes we observed included reimplementing file-local parsers, changing “allow list” logic to “deny list” logic, and other similar changes. 

Conversely, LLM-generated patches did not resolve the vulnerability, added a new vulnerability, or both, an average 53.9% of the time. You can read further details about our findings, observations, and conclusions in the research paper we’ve published alongside this post.

Targeted vulnerabilities

In order to validate the efficacy of LLM-generated patches, we targeted six recently disclosed, novel vulnerabilities in open source software that required complex patch implementations in order to fully resolve the underlying issue(s). The vulnerabilities used to assess patch efficacy included: 

  • CVE-2026-31431 - Linux privilege escalation (“Copy Fail”)

  • CVE-2026-34197 - ActiveMQ Remote Code Execution

  • CVE-2026-8512 - Use-after-free in Chrome's File System Access API on macOS

  • CVE-2026-45185 - EXIM unauthenticated Remote Code Execution

  • CVE-2026-22738 - SpringAI SpEL Remote Code Execution

  • GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g - Gemini CLI Remote Code Execution

Given that open source code is highly likely to exist within the training datasets of frontier models, we specifically chose these vulnerabilities based on the recency of their disclosures, since they and their associated patches were unlikely to be included as part of current models’ training data. Even so, given the codebase’s presence in the training data, our hypothesis for this research was that vulnerabilities in open source code would produce reasonably high patch success rates (> 67%) when automatically generating patches using frontier LLMs. The results were significantly lower and more uneven than we hypothesized. 

For further details on the patch success rates of each model per vulnerability, please see the research paper published alongside this post.

Methodology and the cost of patching

With each model, we generated 540 patches per vulnerability. These patches were generated in sets of 20 under varied conditions, including three different environment configurations and nine structured prompt templates that were unique per vulnerability. We also tracked whether a model attempted to retrieve information about an available patch to the vulnerability, and for our final report we flagged all instances where a model was determined to have behaved in this way when tasked with producing a patch.

With the flagged patches removed, we qualified patch outcomes across five scenarios:

  • Scenario 1 (S1): Complete fix; does not alter application behavior

  • Scenario 2 (S2): Complete fix; alters application behavior

  • Scenario 3 (S3): Does not fix the vulnerability

  • Scenario 4 (S4): Complete fix of the old vulnerability while adding a new vulnerability

  • Scenario 5 (S5): Does not fix the vulnerability while adding a new vulnerability

Figure 1: Average patch success rate across 6,080 patches, with 400 flagged patches removed from reporting.

The inference cost for OpenAI’s ChatGPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber guardrails and the default “medium” effort setting was an average $2.11 per attempted patch and validation cycle. Likewise, the cost for Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 with Cyber Verification Program guardrails and the default “high” effort setting was an average $2.81 per attempted patch and validation cycle.

While these costs might seem trivial compared to the human cost of producing an effective patch, the likely outcome of producing such a patch without altering application behavior was nearly 1 in 4. In other words, LLM-produced patches still require review from a skilled engineer with domain expertise to ensure they actually achieve the desired mitigation(s) without altering application behavior. 

In addition to the corresponding research paper, we are releasing the full set of generated patches, along with the software we designed to generate, validate, compare, and manually verify these patches. As you will see from the patches in the dataset, the difference between a successful patch and one that alters application behavior, leaves the vulnerability unresolved, or even introduces a new vulnerability is quite often fragile, and not always clear at a glance.

In our experiments, more than 33% of the S1 and S2 patches generated by an LLM contained subtleties that we would qualify as “fragile” from a security context. These patches guard against vulnerable inputs with narrowly targeted checks, rather than fully addressing the underlying vulnerable code. For instance, when tasked with patching the SpringAI CVE, both models frequently generated patches that simply escaped specific characters in user input. The patch thus blocked the malicious input string used in the proof-of-concept presented to the model, while leaving the root cause of the vulnerability entirely untouched. If the guarded code were to become reachable again by using alternative inputs, it would lead to the old vulnerability resurfacing in the software. 

Recommendations for improving patch outcomes

We recognize that the outcomes of our research creates a challenge for defenders who are struggling to address a tsunami of vulnerability reports. As such, we reached out to the Frontier AI labs whose models we studied for feedback and recommendations regarding further research. Below is the feedback provided, along with some of our thoughts on what comes next.

Feedback and recommendations from Anthropic: patch generation has outpaced patch verification, and the fix is to make verification execution-grounded rather than inspection-based, while keeping domain experts as the final reviewers at current model capabilities. We've made this point publicly: "Progress on software security used to be limited by how quickly we could find new vulnerabilities. Now it's limited by how quickly we can verify, disclose, and patch." (Project Glasswing initial update, May 2026)

Additional thoughts from 1Password: based on the results of our research, we strongly agree with Anthropic’s feedback on keeping domain experts in the loop as a final reviewer given current model capabilities. We greatly appreciate Anthropic’s review of our research, and the extensive feedback they provided for further consideration in future research.

Final thoughts

Our recommendation today is to leverage the FLAWED tooling we’ve released in order to determine how effective LLMs are at patching vulnerabilities in your organization’s codebase. At the very least, a sample of patches produced by multiple LLMs on previously-patched vulnerabilities will provide leading indicators for where human expertise still provides the greatest impact, while highlighting areas within your codebase that are not well suited to LLM-generated patching alone.

This research casts a spotlight on how LLMs are asymmetrically changing the balance of the “defender’s dilemma” in the attacker’s favor. As the old saying goes: “an attacker only needs to be right once; a defender needs to be right 100% of the time.” These results paint a troubling picture: LLMs that excel at discovering a wide range of vulnerabilities today are only currently effective at patching a narrow subset of them. Having said that, we have identified opportunities for further research that may yet yield more consistent and robust AI-generated patches.

We believe that the software we’ve released, along with the datasets which include all 6,480 patches we generated, will help developers identify scenarios where AI is likely to produce positive outcomes, or at least to steer them away from situations where AI is likely to generate S4 or S5 patches. In the Case Study section of our research paper, we’ve included one such example where our tooling would have helped defenders identify the limitations of AI-generated patching.

Defenders are once again facing the “mechanic’s dilemma” where they must choose between good, fast, and cheap solutions to address this problem. Producing reliable LLM-generated patches may involve some mix of introducing non-LLM tooling, improving test suite robustness, and/or implementing an AI harness to test for invariants. In the interim, our research shows that human expertise still plays an essential role in the process of fully resolving vulnerabilities in software without introducing unwanted side effects. And even then, humans may still fall victim to cognitive surrender if they are not paying careful attention to the code being generated by LLMs.

Special thanks to Casey Ellis, Jason Haddix, Mike Shema and others for their peer review of our research.

blocks.html_en: Given that open source code is highly likely to exist within the training datasets of frontier models, we specifically chose these vulnerabilities based on the recency of their disclosures, since they and their associated patches were unlikely to be included as part of current models’ training data. Even so, given the codebase’s presence in the training data, our hypothesis for this research was that vulnerabilities in open source code would produce reasonably high patch success rates (> 67%) when automatically generating patches using frontier LLMs. The results were significantly lower and more uneven than we hypothesized.

sentences.en: Given that open source code is highly likely to exist within the training datasets of frontier models, we specifically chose these vulnerabilities based on the recency of their disclosures, since they and their associated patches were unlikely to be included as part of current models’ training data.
sentences.zh: 鉴于开源代码很可能存在于前沿模型的训练数据集中，我们根据其披露的新近程度专门选择了这些漏洞，因为它们及其相关补丁不太可能包含在当前模型的训练数据中。

sentences.en: Even so, given the codebase’s presence in the training data, our hypothesis for this research was that vulnerabilities in open source code would produce reasonably high patch success rates (> 67%) when automatically generating patches using frontier LLMs.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，考虑到代码库存在于训练数据中，我们对这项研究的假设是，当使用前沿 LLM 自动生成补丁时，开源代码中的漏洞会产生相当高的补丁成功率 (> 67%)。

sentences.en: The results were significantly lower and more uneven than we hypothesized.
sentences.zh: 结果比我们假设的要低得多，而且更不均匀。

blocks.html_en: With each model, we generated 540 patches per vulnerability. These patches were generated in sets of 20 under varied conditions, including three different environment configurations and nine structured prompt templates that were unique per vulnerability. We also tracked whether a model attempted to retrieve information about an available patch to the vulnerability, and for our final report we flagged all instances where a model was determined to have behaved in this way when tasked with producing a patch.

sentences.en: With each model, we generated 540 patches per vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 对于每个模型，我们为每个漏洞生成了 540 个补丁。

sentences.en: These patches were generated in sets of 20 under varied conditions, including three different environment configurations and nine structured prompt templates that were unique per vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 这些补丁是在不同条件下以 20 个为一组生成的，包括三种不同的环境配置和每个漏洞都是唯一的九个结构化提示模板。

sentences.en: We also tracked whether a model attempted to retrieve information about an available patch to the vulnerability, and for our final report we flagged all instances where a model was determined to have behaved in this way when tasked with producing a patch.
sentences.zh: 我们还跟踪了模型是否尝试检索有关漏洞的可用补丁的信息，并且在最终报告中，我们标记了模型在负责生成补丁时被确定以这种方式表现的所有实例。

blocks.html_en: The inference cost for OpenAI’s ChatGPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber guardrails and the default “medium” effort setting was an average $2.11 per attempted patch and validation cycle. Likewise, the cost for Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 with Cyber Verification Program guardrails and the default “high” effort setting was an average $2.81 per attempted patch and validation cycle.

sentences.en: The inference cost for OpenAI’s ChatGPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber guardrails and the default “medium” effort setting was an average $2.11 per attempted patch and validation cycle.
sentences.zh: OpenAI 的 ChatGPT-5.5 具有网络护栏可信访问和默认的“中等”工作量设置，每次尝试修补和验证周期的推理成本平均为 2.11 美元。

sentences.en: Likewise, the cost for Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 with Cyber Verification Program guardrails and the default “high” effort setting was an average $2.81 per attempted patch and validation cycle.
sentences.zh: 同样，带有网络验证程序护栏和默认“高”工作量设置的 Anthropic Opus 4.8 的平均成本为每次尝试修补和验证周期 2.81 美元。

blocks.html_en: While these costs might seem trivial compared to the human cost of producing an effective patch, the likely outcome of producing such a patch without altering application behavior was nearly 1 in 4. In other words, LLM-produced patches still require review from a skilled engineer with domain expertise to ensure they actually achieve the desired mitigation(s) without altering application behavior.

sentences.en: While these costs might seem trivial compared to the human cost of producing an effective patch, the likely outcome of producing such a patch without altering application behavior was nearly 1 in 4.
sentences.zh: 虽然与生成有效补丁的人力成本相比，这些成本似乎微不足道，但在不改变应用程序行为的情况下生成此类补丁的可能结果接近四分之一。

sentences.en: In other words, LLM-produced patches still require review from a skilled engineer with domain expertise to ensure they actually achieve the desired mitigation(s) without altering application behavior.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，LLM 生成的补丁仍然需要具有领域专业知识的熟练工程师进行审查，以确保它们在不改变应用程序行为的情况下真正实现所需的缓解措施。

blocks.html_en: In addition to the corresponding research paper, we are releasing the full set of generated patches, along with the software we designed to generate, validate, compare, and manually verify these patches. As you will see from the patches in the dataset, the difference between a successful patch and one that alters application behavior, leaves the vulnerability unresolved, or even introduces a new vulnerability is quite often fragile, and not always clear at a glance.

sentences.en: In addition to the corresponding research paper, we are releasing the full set of generated patches, along with the software we designed to generate, validate, compare, and manually verify these patches.
sentences.zh: 除了相应的研究论文之外，我们还发布了全套生成的补丁，以及我们设计用于生成、验证、比较和手动验证这些补丁的软件。

sentences.en: As you will see from the patches in the dataset, the difference between a successful patch and one that alters application behavior, leaves the vulnerability unresolved, or even introduces a new vulnerability is quite often fragile, and not always clear at a glance.
sentences.zh: 正如您从数据集中的补丁中看到的那样，成功的补丁与改变应用程序行为、未解决漏洞甚至引入新漏洞的补丁之间的区别通常很脆弱，并且并不总是一目了然。

blocks.html_en: In our experiments, more than 33% of the S1 and S2 patches generated by an LLM contained subtleties that we would qualify as “fragile” from a security context. These patches guard against vulnerable inputs with narrowly targeted checks, rather than fully addressing the underlying vulnerable code. For instance, when tasked with patching the SpringAI CVE, both models frequently generated patches that simply escaped specific characters in user input. The patch thus blocked the malicious input string used in the proof-of-concept presented to the model, while leaving the root cause of the vulnerability entirely untouched. If the guarded code were to become reachable again by using alternative inputs, it would lead to the old vulnerability resurfacing in the software.

sentences.en: In our experiments, more than 33% of the S1 and S2 patches generated by an LLM contained subtleties that we would qualify as “fragile” from a security context.
sentences.zh: 在我们的实验中，LLM 生成的 S1 和 S2 补丁中超过 33% 包含我们从安全上下文中定义为“脆弱”的微妙之处。

sentences.en: These patches guard against vulnerable inputs with narrowly targeted checks, rather than fully addressing the underlying vulnerable code.
sentences.zh: 这些补丁通过有针对性的检查来防范易受攻击的输入，而不是完全解决底层的易受攻击的代码。

sentences.en: For instance, when tasked with patching the SpringAI CVE, both models frequently generated patches that simply escaped specific characters in user input.
sentences.zh: 例如，当负责修补 SpringAI CVE 时，这两个模型经常生成补丁，这些补丁只是转义用户输入中的特定字符。

sentences.en: The patch thus blocked the malicious input string used in the proof-of-concept presented to the model, while leaving the root cause of the vulnerability entirely untouched.
sentences.zh: 因此，该补丁阻止了向模型提供的概念验证中使用的恶意输入字符串，同时完全未触及漏洞的根本原因。

sentences.en: If the guarded code were to become reachable again by using alternative inputs, it would lead to the old vulnerability resurfacing in the software.
sentences.zh: 如果通过使用替代输入再次可以访问受保护的代码，则会导致旧的漏洞在软件中重新出现。

blocks.html_en: We recognize that the outcomes of our research creates a challenge for defenders who are struggling to address a tsunami of vulnerability reports. As such, we reached out to the Frontier AI labs whose models we studied for feedback and recommendations regarding further research. Below is the feedback provided, along with some of our thoughts on what comes next.

sentences.en: We recognize that the outcomes of our research creates a challenge for defenders who are struggling to address a tsunami of vulnerability reports.
sentences.zh: 我们认识到，我们的研究结果给正在努力应对海量漏洞报告的防御者带来了挑战。

sentences.en: As such, we reached out to the Frontier AI labs whose models we studied for feedback and recommendations regarding further research.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们联系了前沿人工智能实验室，我们研究了该实验室的模型，以获取有关进一步研究的反馈和建议。

sentences.en: Below is the feedback provided, along with some of our thoughts on what comes next.
sentences.zh: 以下是提供的反馈，以及我们对接下来的事情的一些想法。

blocks.html_en: Feedback and recommendations from Anthropic: patch generation has outpaced patch verification, and the fix is to make verification execution-grounded rather than inspection-based, while keeping domain experts as the final reviewers at current model capabilities. We've made this point publicly: "Progress on software security used to be limited by how quickly we could find new vulnerabilities. Now it's limited by how quickly we can verify, disclose, and patch." (Project Glasswing initial update, May 2026)

sentences.en: Feedback and recommendations from Anthropic: patch generation has outpaced patch verification, and the fix is to make verification execution-grounded rather than inspection-based, while keeping domain experts as the final reviewers at current model capabilities.

sentences.en: We've made this point publicly: "Progress on software security used to be limited by how quickly we could find new vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 我们公开指出了这一点：“软件安全方面的进步过去受到我们发现新漏洞的速度的限制。

sentences.en: Now it's limited by how quickly we can verify, disclose, and patch."
sentences.zh: 现在它受到我们验证、披露和修补的速度的限制。”

sentences.en: (Project Glasswing initial update, May 2026)

blocks.html_en: Additional thoughts from 1Password: based on the results of our research, we strongly agree with Anthropic’s feedback on keeping domain experts in the loop as a final reviewer given current model capabilities. We greatly appreciate Anthropic’s review of our research, and the extensive feedback they provided for further consideration in future research.

blocks.html_en: Our recommendation today is to leverage the FLAWED tooling we’ve released in order to determine how effective LLMs are at patching vulnerabilities in your organization’s codebase. At the very least, a sample of patches produced by multiple LLMs on previously-patched vulnerabilities will provide leading indicators for where human expertise still provides the greatest impact, while highlighting areas within your codebase that are not well suited to LLM-generated patching alone.

sentences.en: Our recommendation today is to leverage the FLAWED tooling we’ve released in order to determine how effective LLMs are at patching vulnerabilities in your organization’s codebase.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的建议是利用我们发布的有缺陷的工具来确定法学硕士在修补组织代码库中的漏洞方面的有效性。

sentences.en: At the very least, a sample of patches produced by multiple LLMs on previously-patched vulnerabilities will provide leading indicators for where human expertise still provides the greatest impact, while highlighting areas within your codebase that are not well suited to LLM-generated patching alone.
sentences.zh: 至少，由多个 LLM 针对先前修补的漏洞生成的补丁样本将提供领先指标，表明人类专业知识仍然能产生最大影响，同时突出显示代码库中不太适合单独由 LLM 生成的修补的区域。

blocks.html_en: This research casts a spotlight on how LLMs are asymmetrically changing the balance of the “defender’s dilemma” in the attacker’s favor. As the old saying goes: “an attacker only needs to be right once; a defender needs to be right 100% of the time.” These results paint a troubling picture: LLMs that excel at discovering a wide range of vulnerabilities today are only currently effective at patching a narrow subset of them. Having said that, we have identified opportunities for further research that may yet yield more consistent and robust AI-generated patches.

sentences.en: This research casts a spotlight on how LLMs are asymmetrically changing the balance of the “defender’s dilemma” in the attacker’s favor.
sentences.zh: 这项研究重点关注了法学硕士如何不对称地改变“防御者困境”的平衡，使之有利于攻击者。

sentences.en: As the old saying goes: “an attacker only needs to be right once; a defender needs to be right 100% of the time.”
sentences.zh: 正如一句老话所说：“攻击者只需正确一次；防御者则需要 100% 正确。”

sentences.en: These results paint a troubling picture: LLMs that excel at discovering a wide range of vulnerabilities today are only currently effective at patching a narrow subset of them.
sentences.zh: 这些结果描绘了一幅令人不安的画面：如今擅长发现各种漏洞的法学硕士目前只能有效地修补其中的一小部分漏洞。

sentences.en: Having said that, we have identified opportunities for further research that may yet yield more consistent and robust AI-generated patches.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们已经确定了进一步研究的机会，这些研究可能会产生更一致、更强大的人工智能生成补丁。

blocks.html_en: We believe that the software we’ve released, along with the datasets which include all 6,480 patches we generated, will help developers identify scenarios where AI is likely to produce positive outcomes, or at least to steer them away from situations where AI is likely to generate S4 or S5 patches. In the Case Study section of our research paper, we’ve included one such example where our tooling would have helped defenders identify the limitations of AI-generated patching.

sentences.en: We believe that the software we’ve released, along with the datasets which include all 6,480 patches we generated, will help developers identify scenarios where AI is likely to produce positive outcomes, or at least to steer them away from situations where AI is likely to generate S4 or S5 patches.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，我们发布的软件以及包含我们生成的所有 6,480 个补丁的数据集将帮助开发人员识别人工智能可能产生积极结果的场景，或者至少引导他们远离人工智能可能生成 S4 或 S5 补丁的情况。

sentences.en: In the Case Study section of our research paper, we’ve included one such example where our tooling would have helped defenders identify the limitations of AI-generated patching.
sentences.zh: 在我们研究论文的案例研究部分，我们提供了一个这样的例子，我们的工具可以帮助防御者识别人工智能生成的补丁的局限性。

blocks.html_en: Defenders are once again facing the “mechanic’s dilemma” where they must choose between good, fast, and cheap solutions to address this problem. Producing reliable LLM-generated patches may involve some mix of introducing non-LLM tooling, improving test suite robustness, and/or implementing an AI harness to test for invariants. In the interim, our research shows that human expertise still plays an essential role in the process of fully resolving vulnerabilities in software without introducing unwanted side effects. And even then, humans may still fall victim to cognitive surrender if they are not paying careful attention to the code being generated by LLMs.

sentences.en: Defenders are once again facing the “mechanic’s dilemma” where they must choose between good, fast, and cheap solutions to address this problem.
sentences.zh: 防御者再次面临“机械师的困境”，他们必须在好的、快速的和廉价的解决方案之间做出选择来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Producing reliable LLM-generated patches may involve some mix of introducing non-LLM tooling, improving test suite robustness, and/or implementing an AI harness to test for invariants.

sentences.en: In the interim, our research shows that human expertise still plays an essential role in the process of fully resolving vulnerabilities in software without introducing unwanted side effects.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，我们的研究表明，在完全解决软件漏洞而不引入不必要的副作用的过程中，人类专业知识仍然发挥着重要作用。

sentences.en: And even then, humans may still fall victim to cognitive surrender if they are not paying careful attention to the code being generated by LLMs.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，如果人类不仔细关注法学硕士生成的代码，他们仍然可能成为认知屈服的受害者。

content_html_zh:
我们研究了当大型语言模型 (LLM) 为最近披露的复杂漏洞生成漏洞补丁时会发生什么。 我们的数据显示，当需要复杂补丁时，法学硕士在 53.9% 的情况下会产生带有嵌入式缺陷 (FLAWED) 的类修复工件。

通过分享我们的研究结果，我们的目标是为防御者提供大规模改善漏洞修复结果所需的工具和方法。 除了这篇博客之外，我们还将发布我们的工具、数据集和深入的研究论文，以分享我们所学到的知识。

随着模型和代理工具现在大规模地执行有影响力的漏洞发现，正如最近 Anthropic 的 Glasswing 项目所见证的那样，防御者自然而然地转向人工智能代理来生成漏洞补丁。 事实上，随着 OpenAI 宣布与众多旨在“修补地球”的合作伙伴合作推出“破晓计划”，这种确切的回应成为 6 月份的头条新闻。

但是，法学硕士在不改变应用程序行为的情况下生成补丁的效果如何？ 他们生成的补丁是否确实缓解了相关漏洞？ 这些补丁引入新漏洞的频率有多高？ 作为 1Password 全新安全研究团队 Off-by-1 Labs 的首个研究项目，我们着手回答这些问题。 该论文的标题是“前沿模型的漏洞补丁经常是 F.L.A.W.E.D.”，与该领域的其他研究不同，这项研究针对的是前沿模型训练数据中不太可能发现的新漏洞，然后运用前沿模型来确定其成功生成补丁的功效。

在最近披露的 6 个 CVE 中，我们使用两个前沿的网络推理模型制作了 6,080 个补丁。 生成完全解决漏洞（没有实质性改变应用程序行为）的补丁的平均成功率仅为 26.0%。 补丁成功解决了漏洞，但在此过程中改变了应用程序的行为，发生率是 20.1%。 我们观察到的应用程序行为变化的示例包括重新实现文件本地解析器、将“允许列表”逻辑更改为“拒绝列表”逻辑以及其他类似的更改。

相反，LLM 生成的补丁没有解决漏洞、添加了新漏洞，或者两者兼而有之，平均有 53.9% 的概率。 您可以在我们与本文一起发表的研究论文中阅读有关我们的发现、观察和结论的更多详细信息。

有针对性的漏洞

为了验证 LLM 生成的补丁的有效性，我们针对开源软件中最近披露的六个新漏洞，这些漏洞需要复杂的补丁实现才能完全解决根本问题。 用于评估补丁功效的漏洞包括：

  • CVE-2026-31431 - Linux 权限提升（“复制失败”）
  • CVE-2026-34197 - ActiveMQ 远程代码执行
  • CVE-2026-8512 - macOS 上 Chrome 的文件系统访问 API 中的释放后使用
  • CVE-2026-45185 - EXIM 未经身份验证的远程代码执行
  • CVE-2026-22738 - SpringAI SpEL 远程代码执行
  • GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g - Gemini CLI 远程代码执行

鉴于开源代码很可能存在于前沿模型的训练数据集中，我们根据其披露的新近程度专门选择了这些漏洞，因为它们及其相关补丁不太可能包含在当前模型的训练数据中。 即便如此，考虑到代码库存在于训练数据中，我们对这项研究的假设是，当使用前沿 LLM 自动生成补丁时，开源代码中的漏洞会产生相当高的补丁成功率 (> 67%)。 结果比我们假设的要低得多，而且更不均匀。

有关每个模型每个漏洞的补丁成功率的更多详细信息，请参阅与本文一起发布的研究论文。

方法论和修补成本

对于每个模型，我们为每个漏洞生成了 540 个补丁。 这些补丁是在不同条件下以 20 个为一组生成的，包括三种不同的环境配置和每个漏洞都是唯一的九个结构化提示模板。 我们还跟踪了模型是否尝试检索有关漏洞的可用补丁的信息，并且在最终报告中，我们标记了模型在负责生成补丁时被确定以这种方式表现的所有实例。

删除标记的补丁后，我们确定了五种情况下的补丁结果：

  • 场景1（S1）：完成修复；不改变应用程序行为
  • 场景2（S2）：完全修复；改变应用程序行为
  • 场景3（S3）：不修复漏洞
  • 场景4（S4）：完成旧漏洞修复，同时添加新漏洞
  • 场景5（S5）：不修复漏洞，同时添加新漏洞

图 1：6,080 个补丁的平均补丁成功率，其中 400 个标记补丁从报告中删除。

OpenAI 的 ChatGPT-5.5 具有网络护栏可信访问和默认的“中等”工作量设置，每次尝试修补和验证周期的推理成本平均为 2.11 美元。 同样，带有网络验证程序护栏和默认“高”工作量设置的 Anthropic Opus 4.8 的平均成本为每次尝试修补和验证周期 2.81 美元。

虽然与生成有效补丁的人力成本相比，这些成本似乎微不足道，但在不改变应用程序行为的情况下生成此类补丁的可能结果接近四分之一。 换句话说，LLM 生成的补丁仍然需要具有领域专业知识的熟练工程师进行审查，以确保它们在不改变应用程序行为的情况下真正实现所需的缓解措施。

除了相应的研究论文之外，我们还发布了全套生成的补丁，以及我们设计用于生成、验证、比较和手动验证这些补丁的软件。 正如您从数据集中的补丁中看到的那样，成功的补丁与改变应用程序行为、未解决漏洞甚至引入新漏洞的补丁之间的区别通常很脆弱，并且并不总是一目了然。

在我们的实验中，LLM 生成的 S1 和 S2 补丁中超过 33% 包含我们从安全上下文中定义为“脆弱”的微妙之处。 这些补丁通过有针对性的检查来防范易受攻击的输入，而不是完全解决底层的易受攻击的代码。 例如，当负责修补 SpringAI CVE 时，这两个模型经常生成补丁，这些补丁只是转义用户输入中的特定字符。 因此，该补丁阻止了向模型提供的概念验证中使用的恶意输入字符串，同时完全未触及漏洞的根本原因。 如果通过使用替代输入再次可以访问受保护的代码，则会导致旧的漏洞在软件中重新出现。

改善补丁效果的建议

我们认识到，我们的研究结果给正在努力应对海量漏洞报告的防御者带来了挑战。 因此，我们联系了前沿人工智能实验室，我们研究了该实验室的模型，以获取有关进一步研究的反馈和建议。 以下是提供的反馈，以及我们对接下来的事情的一些想法。

来自 Anthropic 的反馈和建议：补丁生成的速度已经超过了补丁验证的速度，解决方案是使验证执行基于而不是基于检查，同时让领域专家作为当前模型功能的最终审核者。 我们公开指出了这一点：“软件安全方面的进步过去受到我们发现新漏洞的速度的限制。 现在它受到我们验证、披露和修补的速度的限制。” （Glasswing 项目初始更新，2026 年 5 月）

1Password 的其他想法：根据我们的研究结果，我们强烈同意 Anthropic 的反馈，即考虑到当前模型的功能，让领域专家作为最终审阅者参与进来。 我们非常感谢 Anthropic 对我们研究的审查，以及他们提供的广泛反馈，以供未来研究中进一步考虑。

最后的想法

我们今天的建议是利用我们发布的有缺陷的工具来确定法学硕士在修补组织代码库中的漏洞方面的有效性。 至少，由多个 LLM 针对先前修补的漏洞生成的补丁样本将提供领先指标，表明人类专业知识仍然能产生最大影响，同时突出显示代码库中不太适合单独由 LLM 生成的修补的区域。

这项研究重点关注了法学硕士如何不对称地改变“防御者困境”的平衡，使之有利于攻击者。 正如一句老话所说：“攻击者只需正确一次；防御者则需要 100% 正确。” 这些结果描绘了一幅令人不安的画面：如今擅长发现各种漏洞的法学硕士目前只能有效地修补其中的一小部分漏洞。 话虽如此，我们已经确定了进一步研究的机会，这些研究可能会产生更一致、更强大的人工智能生成补丁。

我们相信，我们发布的软件以及包含我们生成的所有 6,480 个补丁的数据集将帮助开发人员识别人工智能可能产生积极结果的场景，或者至少引导他们远离人工智能可能生成 S4 或 S5 补丁的情况。 在我们研究论文的案例研究部分，我们提供了一个这样的例子，我们的工具可以帮助防御者识别人工智能生成的补丁的局限性。

防御者再次面临“机械师的困境”，他们必须在好的、快速的和廉价的解决方案之间做出选择来解决这个问题。 生成可靠的 LLM 生成的补丁可能需要引入非 LLM 工具、提高测试套件的稳健性和/或实施 AI 工具来测试不变量。 在此期间，我们的研究表明，在完全解决软件漏洞而不引入不必要的副作用的过程中，人类专业知识仍然发挥着重要作用。 即便如此，如果人类不仔细关注法学硕士生成的代码，他们仍然可能成为认知屈服的受害者。
